page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a GPU-accelerated server configured with two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. The host system features an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. System memory consists of 375.0 GB of RAM, yielding 11.72 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 2200 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in LLM inference workloads. For a medium 7B model, the server achieves prompt processing speeds of 6275.36 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 141.42 tokens per second. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also reaches top-tier status at 15.2 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 62892.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 64768.69. Memory read bandwidth is strong at 4985.78 GB/sec for small cached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is average at 88.2 GB/sec.

This server offers high resource density by combining dedicated compute cores, substantial system memory, and dual enterprise GPUs. The qualitative cost efficiency is high for workloads requiring parallel GPU processing and large memory footprints, as the hardware profile reduces the need for multi-node clustering. However, a tradeoff exists in single-core CPU performance, which registers as average with a stress-ng single-core score of 2209.29, indicating that highly sequential, non-parallelized CPU tasks may not fully leverage the hardware's value.

The server is configured for GPU-accelerated workloads, specifically LLM inference, machine learning model training, and data science pipelines. The combination of 375.0 GB of RAM and a 2200 GB NVMe SSD also makes it suitable for large-scale database operations, high-throughput static web serving, and parallelized cryptographic or decompression tasks.
